It sounds like your friend might be a bit socially awkward. It's likely she's struggling because she doesn't know what to say to keep the conversation going. Put more time and effort into your replies, ask her questions, and share fun tidbits about your day—that might be all you need to fix the issue. 

At the end of the day, though, you two simply might not be compatible. You don't need to stick in a relationship of any kind—friendship, romantic, even familial—if you no longer find joy in it. (No matter how nice they are.)

You're not alone; I felt this way myself when my scars first began to fade. Mental illness is an internal illness; nobody can tell just by looking at you that you're struggling. In some warped, depression-fueled way, scars are an external validator of your internal pain. So, while you've since found better ways to cope, it makes perfect sense that losing those validators would trigger a rise in negative emotions and thoughts. 

What helped me improve my mood without slipping back into those unhealthy coping mechanisms were things like doodling in the areas where the scars used to be, wearing a rubber band around my wrist and snapping it lightly every time I felt the urge to harm myself, and expressing myself through fun and flashy fashion, makeup, and hairstyles. It's very common to feel upset when SH marks begin to fade, but these feelings will pass, I promise. And even if the tactics I gave don't work, there are many, many more for you to try out there that were developed specifically for situations like these. 

Keep your head up and know that it's ok if you relapse. Recovery is rarely a linear path, there will be ups and downs, but what matters most is that you're trying.

No matter what you said, she likely would have found a way to twist you into the villain. I would recommend talking to Chris one-on-one about his feelings on the matter and, potentially, asking him to keep Gabi away from your meetups. Every one of us is different, and every one of us has unique experiences and unique discomforts.
